the discursive (de) legitimation of a contested investment project involves three types of struggles, namely, legalistic argumentation that is based on technical and environmental evaluations and that emphasizes corporate expertise; truth fights that are based on the use of scientific knowledge; and political battles that involve the mobilization of political resources and political actors.
the media discourse on the Finnish pulp mill in Uruguay was characterized by legalistic argumentation and by truth fights and political battles.

the media coverage of Metsa-Botnias world-scale pulp mill project in Uruguay was characterized by a struggle to establish or deestablish legitimacy of the company, and that the company representatives attempted to establish their legitimacy by framing the issue in legal and technical terms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the discursive (de) legitimating practices of corporate actors and their allies in the context of a contested corporate undertaking.
the question of how social actors struggle to define the social role and responsibility and to establish the legitimacy of corporations in the context of socially contested projects.
how the corporate social responsibility discourse can be used as an instrument for the (de)legitmation of corporate actions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
corporate social responsibility is not a matter of a few good deeds, but a complex and multifaceted social and political process that involves a wide range of actors, issues, and struggles.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the media is a powerful tool for corporate representatives and their allies in the struggle for legitimacy.

the corporate actors, with the help of media, are able to frame their activities in a positive light by emphasizing the legal, scientific, technical and environmental dimensions, and by distancing themselves from the political dimension of corporate social responsibility debates.

we have shown how the corporate representatives and the media tend to construct the corporate role and responsibility in a way that is favorable to the corporation and that is in line with corporate social responsibility discourse.
The main takeaway from our work is that
critical discursive analysis is a promising method for investigating subtle meaning-making processes and the struggle for legitimacy in corporate social responsibilities debates.

the struggle over legitimacy is a complex discursive process, and that the discursive strategies used in this process have important implications for the ways in which corporate social responsibility issues are framed and understood.
the discursive struggle over legitimacy is an important part of the corporate social responsibility process, and that the media can be a powerful ally in this struggle.
